shared_elements: low-relief carving on weathered pale stone
horizontal register or band separating carved zones
row of repeated figures in profile along a band
figures shown in strict profile view
outdoor stone masonry / rubble setting under open sky
justification: Both are weathered stone surfaces carved in low relief and both use a horizontal band filled with a row of repeated profile figures (a procession of humans in A, a line of crouching creatures along the top of B), and both are photographed in situ amid rubble under sky. Beyond that generic frieze principle they diverge sharply: A is a single continuous, finely modelled and proportioned human procession on a long orthostat wall, while B is a tall isolated slab with schematic, shallow, disparately scaled animals stacked in vertical zones, rendered in a far cruder manner.
